text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Wednesday.

GERMANY - Bund futures were sharply lower as a slew of economic reports appeared on balance to not be as negative as traders had expected. The June DTB Bund futures contract was down 45 basis points late in the day at 102.11 and had traded as low as 101.85. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 103.06, down 0.22 from Tuesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts were under pressure, following spooked Bunds downward to end near session lows. UK base rates were unchanged at 6.0 percent as expected. Market awaits Fed's Greenspan testimony before Congress at 1700 GMT, Friday's U.S. non-farm payrolls. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 111-12/32, down 23/32 from Tuesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - March bond future slipped to lowest level since Feb 10 with Bunds. Technical support levels feature of day, OAT auction weighing and talk of switching to equities not helping. The March notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 131.52 down 0.6 from Tuesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bond futures continue to slip through the day to show losses of nearly a full point in late afternoon reflecting lower German bunds and U.S. Treasuries, and against background doubts that a European single currency will start on time. Markets generally cautious ahead of second leg of Greenspan's testimony and ahead of Friday's U.S. jobs data. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 127.78 down 0.22 from Tuesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries were gaining midmorning, flat to higher. Greenspan says earnings may validate stock prices. Fed chief's comments provide upward impetus for stocks, bonds. Market awaits second leg of Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony at 1400 EST/1900 GMT. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 110-07/32, down 03/32 from Tuesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.87 percent.

JAPAN - Japanese goverment bonds (JGB) futures ended slightly lower after trading in narrow ranges. Dealers liquidated longs following chief government spokesman's remarks that Japan needs to consider measures to deal with adverse impact of low interest rates.In after hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 126.39, up 0.07 from Tuesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary market saw deals in sterling, marks, rand and Czech crowns on Wednesday with little dollar activity ahead of U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey- Hawkins testimony. In sterling, the World Bank launched a 300 million stg three-year bond and Fannie Mae increased a June 2002 bond. The World Bank and KfW tapped the Czech crown sector. There was also activity in the rand sector with the World Bank launching a 2.5 billion rand 20-year zero-coupon bond.
